newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFI 15 has four more bourse candidates.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFI 15 has four more bourse candidates.

text.p: Poland's National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 15 in the country's mass privatisation programme has four more bourse candidates after shares in wood firm Grajewo SA, were approved for public trade on Thursday.

"We have other candidates which...will be ready for the bourse next year or over the next two years," Krzysztof Sedzikowski, president of the fund's management firm Creditanstalt-SCG, told a news conference.

Sedzikowski said the firms were meat producer Zaklady Miesne Ostroda-Morliny SA, chemical-resistant equipment maker Zaklady Aparatury Chemicznej Chemet SA, shoe firm Zlotoryjskie Zaklady Obuwia SA and carpet maker Fabryka Dywanow Kowary SA.
On Thursday the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) approved for public trade shares in Zaklady Plyt Wiorowych Grajewo SA, which plans a December public offering.
Under the NFI scheme shares in some 500 companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.
So far more than 22 million of of Poland's 28.5 million adults have picked up mass privatisation units which will later be exchanged for shares of the NFIs and which are on sale until November 22.
